KEY MESSAGE 1...
A low pressure system off the Atlantic Coast continues to slowly 
head eastward today. As the weather system heads slowly eastward, 
there are medium chances (40-50 percent) for light isolated to 
scattered rain showers through this afternoon across eastern New 
York and medium to high chances (greater than 50 percent) across 
western New England. Now, the nature of rain showers will be 
much lighter compared to what have observed over the last two 
days. Rainfall amounts are forecasted to range between 0.05 
inches and 0.25 inches for today. 

Based on the latest National Blend of Model data and high 
resolution model guidances, there are low chances for an 
isolated non-severe thunderstorm this afternoon primarily 
between 2 PM and 7 PM across western New England and portions of
eastern New York. For locations that could observe a 
thunderstorm this afternoon, locally higher rainfall amounts 
could reach up to 0.5 inches. We are starting to lose enough 
moisture and energy for any higher rainfall amounts as the low 
pressure system continues to head eastward today and strong 
surface high pressure continues to move in from the Great Lakes 
region. 

While the heaviest rainfall has ended, rivers, streams, and 
creeks are still responding to our most recent heavy rainfall 
across eastern New York today and into tonight. Along the Hoosic
River at Eagle Bridge, minor flooding is occurring with timing 
of cresting by 8 AM this morning (or sooner). Rivers, streams, 
and creeks in eastern New York (outside of the southern 
Adirondacks and Lake George-Saratoga region) will still be
running high through the day today. The additional rainfall 
today will be on the lighter side to contribute very little to 
any on-going minor flooding. Drier conditions are in store for
late tonight into tomorrow morning for rivers, streams, and
creeks to begin returning to near normal levels. Continue to 
follow all local law enforcement road closures and never drive 
through flooded roadways. 

KEY MESSAGE 2...
Latest ensemble forecast models continue to support an upper level 
trough moving through eastern New York and western New England 
Sunday afternoon into Monday. This brings increasing confidence for 
widespread rain showers Sunday afternoon through Monday morning. 
There are some fluctuations with the ensemble members on where the 
axis of heavy rainfall could occur. The best case scenario and 
currently supported by the latest forecast is for the highest 
rainfall totals to be to our north and west with that potential for 
heavy rainfall. For across eastern New York and western New England, 
latest probabilities from the National Blend of Model data for 24 
hour precipitation totals from 2 PM Sunday to 2 PM Monday exceeding 
1 inch are between 30 and 40 percent. For precipitation totals 
reaching or exceeding 0.5 inches is between 60 and 70 percent. 
Confidence is higher for widespread totals to be between 0.25 inches 
and 0.5 inches. The latest forecast supports medium chances for 
isolated thunderstorms during the evening and early overnight 
hours across eastern New York and western New England. While the
severity and exact timing of storms are uncertain at this 
forecast time, one or two stronger storms could develop with 
primary concern being strong winds as the latest forecast 
supports enough ingredients needed for thunderstorms to develop.
We will continue to monitor the forecast trends and keep up to 
date with the latest forecast as we get closer to Sunday. 

At this forecast time, confidence for higher rainfall totals is for 
the best case scenario for higher totals (of up to 1 inch) in the 
southern Adirondacks and Lake George-Saratoga regions. With this 
information, flash flooding concerns are low as mostly dry 
conditions are in store for Friday into Sunday morning and soil 
conditions will have time to dry before our next batch of rainfall 
moves in.
